materials.prompt: のも当然だ
materials.answer:
it's only natural that ~; no wonder ~

〜のも当然だ means 'it's only natural that ~ / no wonder ~' — given the circumstances, the result or reaction is entirely to be expected. あれだけ練習したのだから、勝つのも当然だ = having practiced that much, of course they'd win. It attaches to a plain-form clause + のも, or to a noun + も.
materials.reading: のもとうぜんだ
materials.notes:
当然 is read とうぜん; the phrase judges a result to be the natural, expected consequence of a stated cause.

It is very close to のももっともだ; 当然だ leans more on 'obviously so', もっともだ on 'reasonable / understandable'.

Synonyms: no-mo-mottomo-da — のももっともだ 'it's understandable that'; のも当然だ stresses that the result is the obvious, expected one.

Related: wake-da — わけだ 'that's why, no wonder'; のも当然だ explicitly labels the outcome as natural or deserved.

Related: hazu-da — はずだ 'should be, expected'; のも当然だ judges a fact as a natural consequence rather than a logical expectation.

Source references: jlptsensei, bunpro

examples.japanese: あれだけひどいことを言われたのだから、彼女が怒るのも当然だ。
examples.english: Having been told something that awful, it's only natural that she got angry.

examples.japanese: 準備を全くしていなかったのだから、失敗するのも当然だった。
examples.english: Since he hadn't prepared at all, it was no wonder he failed.
examples.reading: じゅんびをまったくしていなかったのだから、しっぱいするのもとうぜんだった。

materials.prompt: の下で
materials.answer:
under; under the supervision / influence of

〜の下で(もとで) means acting 'under' someone or something — under their guidance, authority, or a set of conditions. 有名な先生の下で学ぶ = study under a famous teacher; 厳しい規則の下で = under strict rules. Here 下 is read もと and means a governing influence or circumstance, not a physical 'below'. の下に is a close variant.
materials.reading: のもとで
materials.notes:
下 here is read もと (not した); it means 'under the influence / authority / conditions of', not physically underneath.

の下で often stresses the activity carried on under that condition; の下に can stress the resulting state or arrangement.

Related: ni-oite — において marks a formal place or situation ('in / at'); の下で marks acting under a person's authority or a condition.

Related: o-moto-ni — をもとに uses もと for a basis or source ('based on ~'); の下で means 'under the authority / conditions of'.

Source references: jlptsensei, bunpro

examples.japanese: 彼は有名な研究者の下で、長年研究を続けてきた。
examples.english: He has continued his research for many years under a famous scholar.
examples.reading: かれはゆうめいなけんきゅうしゃのもとで、ながねんけんきゅうをつづけてきた。

examples.japanese: 厳しい規則の下で、選手たちは日々練習に励んでいる。
examples.english: Under strict rules, the athletes devote themselves to practice day after day.
examples.reading: きびしいきそくのもとで、せんしゅたちはひびれんしゅうにはげんでいる。

materials.prompt: の中で
materials.answer:
among; in (a group or category)

の中で marks a group or category as the field you are picking from or comparing within: 'among ~ / of all ~'. クラスの中で = among the class, 四季の中で = of the four seasons. It sets the scope, so it very often pairs with 一番 to single out the top member of that group.
materials.reading: のなかで
materials.notes:
For a group of concrete items, で after の中 is standard (クラスの中で). で (rather than に) fits because a comparison is being made within that scope.

This 中 is read なか, not じゅう/ちゅう; it means 'within the set', not 'throughout a time'.

Related: no-naka-de-ichiban — 〜の中で〜が一番〜 is the full superlative frame this phrase forms the first half of.

Related: ichiban — 一番 picks the top item; の中で names the group it is picked from.

Source references: jlptsensei, bunpro

examples.japanese: クラスの中で、田中さんが一番背が高いです。
examples.english: In the class, Tanaka is the tallest.
examples.reading: クラスのなかで、たなかさんがいちばんせがたかいです。

examples.japanese: 四季の中で、秋が一番好きです。
examples.english: Of the four seasons, I like autumn the most.
examples.reading: しきのなかで、あきがいちばんすきです。

materials.prompt: 〜の中で〜が一番
materials.answer:
the most ~ in (a group)

This pattern picks the top member of a defined group: の中で marks the range or category, and が一番 plus an adjective names what stands out the most. It is the everyday way to make a superlative statement about a set of things.
materials.reading: のなかでがいちばん
materials.notes:
Use の中で to compare within a whole category; when choosing between just two items, use 〜と〜とどちら instead.

一番 here means "number one / the most", turning the adjective into a superlative.

Related: ichiban — 一番 is the superlative word this pattern is built around.

Related: yori-hou-ga — より〜のほうが compares two items; の中で〜が一番 ranks the top of a whole group.

Related: wa-yori-desu — は〜より…です compares two nouns directly, without singling out a group's best.

Source references: jlptsensei, bunpro
structures: Noun［group］＋ の中で ＋ Noun ＋ が ＋ 一番 ＋ い-adjective／な-adjective

examples.english: Of all fruits, I like apples the most.
examples.reading: くだもののなかでりんごがいちばんすきです。

examples.english: In the class, Tanaka is the tallest.

materials.prompt: 〜のなんのって
materials.answer:
so ~ that words fail; incredibly ~

〜のなんのって is a very colloquial way to exaggerate a degree — 寒いのなんのって = it was so unbelievably cold, words can't capture it. It follows an い-adjective or plain-form verb and is usually left trailing, inviting the listener to imagine just how extreme it was. This belongs to casual, spoken Japanese and carries a lively, emphatic tone.
materials.reading: のなんのって
materials.notes:
This is casual spoken emphasis; it clashes with the formal register of の極み or の至り.

It often trails off after the exaggeration, leaving the degree to the listener's imagination.

Synonyms: koto-ka — ことか is an emotive 'how ~!' that works in writing; のなんのって is strictly casual, spoken exaggeration.

Source references: jlptsensei, bunpro

examples.japanese: 山頂の風が冷たいのなんのって、じっと立っていられなかった。
examples.english: The wind at the summit was so unbelievably cold I couldn't stand still.

materials.prompt: の
materials.answer:
the act of ~ (nominalizer)

Placing の after a plain verb or clause turns that whole idea into a noun, so it can then take particles like が, を, or は. You reach for it to talk about doing something as a thing in itself, especially with verbs of perception such as 見る and 聞く.
materials.reading: の
materials.notes:
For things you perceive directly (見る, 聞く) use の; for abstract or reported ideas (言う, 思う) こと is more natural.

Don't confuse this nominalizing の with the explanatory の at the end of casual questions — this one sits in the middle of the sentence and carries a particle.

Synonyms: koto — こと also nominalizes; の suits perceived, concrete events while こと suits abstract or stated ones.

Related: no-ga-suki — のが好き is built on this nominalizing の plus が好き.

Related: no-substitute — の as "one" replaces a known noun, whereas this の repackages a whole clause.

Source references: bunpro

materials.prompt: の
materials.answer:
's; of (noun-linking)

The particle の joins two nouns so the first one describes or owns the second, like English "'s" or "of". It covers possession, belonging, and general relationships, and the describing noun always comes first: 私の本 is "my book".
materials.reading: の
materials.notes:
The order is fixed: the modifier goes before の. 私の本 means "my book", while 本の私 makes no sense.

Japanese needs の between two nouns where English can just stack them — 日本語の先生 ("a teacher of Japanese"), not 日本語先生.

You can chain several: 友達のお父さんの車 ("my friend's father's car").

Related: no-substitute — The same の can stand in for a noun as "one", dropping the second noun.

Related: no-nominalizer — の also turns a whole verb clause into a noun, a different job from linking two nouns.

Related: ga-no-conversion — Inside a noun-modifying clause, this same の can replace が as the subject marker.

Source references: jlptsensei, bunpro

materials.prompt: の
materials.answer:
one (a known noun)

の can stand in for a noun that both speakers already understand, exactly like English "one" in "the red one". It lets you drop a repeated noun and just describe the choice with an adjective.
materials.reading: の
materials.notes:
After a な-adjective, insert な before の: 静かなの ("a quiet one").

Don't repeat the noun after の — 赤いの already means "the red one", so 赤いの本 is wrong.

Synonyms: adjective-no — の as "one" after an adjective is the very same usage seen from the adjective side.

Related: no-possession — The possessive/linking の joins two nouns; this の replaces a noun altogether.

Related: no-nominalizer — Both hide a noun, but the nominalizer packages a whole action rather than a single 'one'.

Source references: bunpro

materials.prompt: の次に
materials.answer:
next after ~; second to ~ (in order or rank)

の次に places one thing right after another in a sequence or ranking: 'next after ~' or 'second to ~'. Noun の次に names the reference point, and what follows is what comes immediately after it — the second-tallest after Mt. Fuji, or the thing you'll do next after English.
materials.reading: のつぎに
materials.notes:
Use の, not を: 英語の次に, not 英語を次に.

For ranking, の次に marks second place behind the top item, so it usually appears alongside a superlative like 一番.

Related: ichiban — 一番 names the outright top; の次に names what stands immediately below it.

Related: no-naka-de — の中で marks the group; の次に orders items within such a ranking.

Source references: bunpro

materials.prompt: のうち(で)
materials.answer:
among; out of; of the (group)

〜のうち(で) marks the group or range from which something is singled out — 'among / out of.' 四人のうちで一番背が高い = the tallest of the four; 一年のうちで = within (the span of) a year. It commonly appears with superlatives or when picking a subset out of a whole, and is close to 〜の中で.
materials.reading: のうちで
materials.notes:
With comparisons it names the set being compared (three of us, this list); it overlaps closely with 〜の中で.

うちに (with に) means 'while / before' a state ends — a different meaning from うち(で) 'among'.

Related: uchi-ni — うちに means 'while / before (a state ends)'; のうちで picks one out of a group.

Source references: bunpro

materials.prompt: の上では
materials.answer:
as far as ~ goes; on paper; in terms of

〜の上では means 'as far as ~ goes / on the level of ~' — judging by a document, calculation, or nominal standard, often implying that reality may differ. 計算の上では = by calculation (in theory); 法律の上では = legally speaking (on paper). It frequently sets up a contrast with how things actually are.
materials.reading: のうえでは
materials.notes:
Here 上 is read うえ and means 'on the level / basis of', not a physical 'on top of'.

It often implies the real situation differs from the stated standard (数字の上では回復したが、実感はない).

Related: ue-de — 〜上で means 'upon doing / in the process of' — a different use of 上; の上では means 'on the nominal level of ~, as opposed to reality'.

Source references: jlptsensei

materials.prompt: のは〜の方だ
materials.answer:
the one who/that ~ is X (it is X that ~)

This pattern singles out which side something is really true of, out of two possibilities. のは names the situation, and 〜の方だ points to the party or option it actually applies to — 謝るのはあなたの方だ = the one who should apologize is you. It often corrects or clarifies who or which is really the case, against a mistaken assumption.
materials.notes:
方 here contrasts one side against another; the pattern works when there are two candidates and you are picking which one it truly applies to.

方 in this pattern reads ほう (the 'side/option' word), not かた ('person/way').

Related: hou-ga-ii — 〜方がいい recommends one option over another; 〜のは〜の方だ points out which side something is actually true of.

Related: no-nominalizer — nominalizing の turns a clause into a noun; this cleft uses that の to spotlight which party a statement applies to.

Source references: bunpro

materials.prompt: 〜のやら・〜ものやら・〜ことやら
materials.answer:
I wonder; who knows (uncertainty)

〜のやら, and its variants 〜ものやら and 〜ことやら, attach to an embedded question to express 'who knows / I wonder', with a musing and often faintly worried tone. どうしたものやら = I have no idea what to do, どこにいることやら = who knows where he is. It usually follows a question word such as どう, どこ, いつ, or 何, and belongs to reflective, slightly literary speech.
materials.reading: のやら・ものやら・ことやら
materials.notes:
It follows a single embedded question and means 'who knows ~'; ものやら・ことやら add a musing or worried undertone.

It typically comes after a question word (どう・どこ・いつ・何) rather than a yes/no clause.

Synonyms: no-yara-no-yara — the paired 〜のやら〜のやら weighs two possibilities; the single 〜のやら／ものやら muses over one open question.

Synonyms: koto-ka — ことか exclaims 'how ~!' with feeling; ことやら wonders aloud with unresolved uncertainty.

Source references: jlptsensei

materials.prompt: 〜のやら〜のやら
materials.answer:
whether ~ or ~ (I can't tell which)

〜のやら〜のやら pairs two possibilities — often opposites — to say the speaker can't tell which is the case. 本当なのやら嘘なのやら = whether it's true or a lie, no telling. It joins two plain-form clauses and frequently takes the shape 〜のやら〜ないのやら ('whether ~ or not'). The tone conveys genuine puzzlement or resignation.
materials.notes:
It lines up two (often opposite) possibilities to say which one holds is unknown; a common shape is 〜のやら〜ないのやら.

The overall feeling is puzzlement or resignation, not a neutral 'either A or B' choice.

Synonyms: no-yara-mono-yara — the single 〜のやら／ものやら expresses one unresolved question; the paired 〜のやら〜のやら weighs two possibilities against each other.

Source references: jlptsensei

materials.prompt: のように・のような
materials.answer:
like (a noun); similar to ~

のように and のような compare something to a noun. Use のように before a verb or adjective (歌手のように歌う = sing like a singer) and のような before a noun (雪のような花 = flowers like snow). The noun before の is the thing being resembled, giving a vivid 'just like ~' comparison.
materials.reading: のように・のような
materials.notes:
Pick the ending by what follows: のように modifies a verb or adjective, のような modifies a noun — 雪のような花, not 雪のように花.

Because のよう attaches to a noun, keep the の: 子どものように, not 子どもように.

Related: mitai-na — みたいに・みたいな is the casual equivalent of のように・のような after a noun.

Related: you-ni-you-na — ように・ような can follow verbs and clauses too; のように・のような attaches specifically to a noun.

Related: you-da — ようだ is the predicate 'seems / is like' form of the same よう.

Source references: bunpro

materials.prompt: ので
materials.answer:
because; since

ので connects a reason to its result, joining the cause clause to the main clause. Compared with から it feels softer and more matter-of-fact, so it is common in polite explanations, excuses, and requests.
materials.reading: ので
materials.notes:
After a な-adjective or a noun, add な before ので: 静かなので, 学生なので.

ので presents the reason as objective and gentle, so it sounds more polite than から when you make an excuse or ask a favor.

Synonyms: kara — から states a reason more directly and personally; ので sounds softer and more polite.

Source references: jlptsensei, bunpro

materials.prompt: のみ
materials.answer:
only; just; nothing but (formal)

のみ is the formal, written-language equivalent of だけ, meaning 'only / just.' 会員のみ = members only; 見守るのみだ = do nothing but watch over. It appears in notices, contracts, and formal prose, while conversation uses だけ. It attaches to nouns and to plain-form verbs.
materials.reading: のみ
materials.notes:
のみ belongs to formal, written style; everyday speech uses だけ.

Do not confuse standalone のみ ('only') with のみならず ('not only ~ but also'), a separate expression.

Synonyms: dake — だけ is the everyday 'only'; のみ is its formal, written equivalent.

Synonyms: shika-nai — しか〜ない 'only, nothing but' requires a negative verb; のみ is affirmative and formal.

Related: nominarazu — のみならず ('not only ~ but also') is built on this のみ.

Source references: jlptsensei, bunpro

materials.prompt: のみならず
materials.answer:
not only ~ but also

のみならず means 'not only ~ but also,' the formal counterpart of だけでなく. It states one fact and then adds a further, often broader one: 国内のみならず海外でも = not only domestically but abroad as well. It attaches to nouns and plain-form clauses, and the second part is frequently marked with も. The register is formal and written.
materials.reading: のみならず
materials.notes:
It is formal and written; conversationally だけでなく is the natural choice.

The added element is usually equal to or larger in scope than the first, often marked with も.

Synonyms: dake-de-naku — だけでなく is the everyday 'not only ~ but also'; のみならず is its formal equivalent.

Synonyms: bakari-ka — ばかりか 'not only ~ but even' highlights an escalating, often surprising addition; のみならず is more neutral and formal.

Synonyms: ni-todomarazu — にとどまらず 'not stopping at ~' stresses going beyond a limit; のみならず simply adds a further element.

Related: wa-mochiron — はもちろん 'not to mention' treats the first item as obvious; のみならず adds a further point in formal prose.

Source references: jlptsensei, bunpro

materials.prompt: のに
materials.answer:
although; even though; despite

This のに links two clauses that clash, adding a feeling of surprise, dissatisfaction, or complaint: 'even though A, B (unexpectedly)'. It follows the plain form; after nouns and な-adjectives, insert な (な-adjective な のに, Noun な のに). Unlike neutral けど, のに carries an emotional 'and yet' that things didn't go as they should have.
materials.reading: のに
materials.notes:
Don't confuse it with the purpose のに ('in order to'); that one follows a dictionary verb and pairs with words like 使う/かかる/必要, with no sense of contrast.

Nouns and な-adjectives need な before のに: 学生なのに, 静かなのに — not 学生のに.

Related: noni-in-order-to — Same shape のに but 'in order to'; it follows a dictionary verb and shows no contrast.

Related: kedo — けど is a neutral 'but'; のに adds surprise or dissatisfaction that the result went against expectation.

Related: temo — ても is 'even if' about a supposed case; のに is 'even though' about something that actually happened.

Source references: jlptsensei, bunpro

materials.prompt: のに
materials.answer:
in order to; for (doing) ~

This のに frames an action as the purpose you are evaluating something against: 'for doing ~ / in order to ~'. It follows a dictionary-form verb and leads into a comment on what that task takes — time, tools, cost, or convenience: 覚えるのに一週間かかった = it took a week to memorize. It commonly appears with 使う, かかる, いる, 必要, 便利.
materials.reading: のに
materials.notes:
Keep the verb in dictionary form: 行くのに, not 行ったのに (that would be the 'although' のに).

This purpose のに suits concrete tasks judged by cost or usefulness. For someone's goal or intention, ために is usually more natural.

bunpro lists N3

Related: noni-although — Same のに shape but 'although'; that one carries contrast and can follow past forms.

Related: tame-ni — ために also means 'in order to'; のに focuses on what a concrete task requires (time, tools, cost).

Related: you-ni-so-that — ように sets an aim with non-volitional verbs; this のに measures effort against a purpose.

Source references: jlptsensei, bunpro

materials.prompt: のは～だ
materials.answer:
it is ~ that ~ (cleft sentence)

のは〜だ builds a cleft sentence that spotlights one part of the idea. Nominalize a clause with の, mark it with は as the known information, and end with the highlighted element plus だ: 私が生まれたのは北海道です = it was in Hokkaido that I was born. It answers 'which / where / who / when' by putting that answer in the だ slot.
materials.notes:
The の here nominalizes the clause; don't drop it — 生まれたのは, not 生まれたは.

The stressed answer lands right before だ. Compare 私が買ったのは本です (what I bought was a book) with a plain 私は本を買いました (I bought a book), which highlights nothing.

Related: no-nominalizer — The の in のは〜だ is the nominalizer, turning a whole clause into a noun that は can mark.

Related: no-explanatory — Explanatory んです explains a situation; のは〜だ instead singles out one element as the focus.

Source references: jlptsensei
structures: Sentence［plain form］ ＋ の ＋ は ＋ Noun／Phrase ＋ だ

materials.prompt: 〜ぬ
materials.answer:
not (classical negative, = ない)

〜ぬ is the classical negative ending, equivalent to modern 〜ない. It attaches to the same stem as ない (知らぬ = 知らない, 思わぬ = 思わない), with the irregular せぬ for する and 来ぬ(こぬ) for 来る. Today it survives mainly in set phrases, proverbs, and a stiff literary or archaic tone (見知らぬ人, 思わぬ結果).
materials.reading: ぬ
materials.notes:
It attaches to the same stem as ない (行かぬ, 知らぬ), and する becomes せぬ, not しぬ.

The colloquial 知らん is a contraction of this 知らぬ／知らない; sentence-final ぬ itself sounds literary or fixed, not everyday speech.

Before a noun it works attributively (見知らぬ土地 = an unfamiliar place).

Synonyms: zaru — 〜ざる is the classical negative used attributively before a noun; ぬ is its plain sentence-ending counterpart, overlapping closely.

Related: zuni — ずに 'without doing' comes from the same classical negative ず; ぬ is the counterpart meaning simply 'not'.

Source references: jlptsensei, bunpro
structures: する → せぬ ／ 来る → 来ぬ（こぬ）

examples.japanese: 世の中には、知らぬほうが幸せなこともある。
examples.english: In this world, there are things you are happier not knowing.
examples.reading: よのなかには、しらぬほうがしあわせなこともある。

examples.japanese: 彼は困っている人を見て、見ぬふりはできなかった。
examples.english: Seeing someone in trouble, he could not just pretend not to notice.
examples.reading: かれはこまっているひとをみて、みぬふりはできなかった。

materials.prompt: 抜きで・抜きにして
materials.answer:
without; leaving out; setting aside

〜抜きで and 〜抜きにして mean doing something while leaving out a normally-expected element. 朝食抜きで = without breakfast; 冗談抜きで = joking aside. 〜は抜きにして ('let's leave ~ out') often opens a suggestion to set something aside. It attaches to a noun. The related 〜を抜きにしては + negative means the following would be impossible without it.
materials.reading: ぬきで・ぬきにして
materials.notes:
It attaches to a noun; to say 'without doing (a verb)', use ないで or ずに, not 抜き.

〜を抜きにしては／抜きには + a negative means the following is impossible without it (彼の協力を抜きにしては成功しなかった).

Synonyms: nashi — 〜なし simply states a noun's absence ('without ~'); 抜き stresses deliberately leaving out something normally included.

Synonyms: nashi-ni — なしに・なしで also means 'without'; 抜きにして often carries the nuance 'let's set aside / omit on purpose'.

Source references: jlptsensei, bunpro
structures: Noun ＋ 抜きで／抜きにして
Noun ＋ を抜きにしては ＋ ～ない

examples.japanese: 今日は堅い話は抜きにして、みんなで楽しく飲みましょう。
examples.english: Let's leave the stiff talk aside today and just enjoy some drinks together.
examples.reading: きょうはかたいはなしはぬきにして、みんなでたのしくのみましょう。

examples.japanese: 地元の人々の協力を抜きにして、この祭りは成り立たない。
examples.english: Without the cooperation of the local people, this festival could not be held.
examples.reading: じもとのひとびとのきょうりょくをぬきにして、このまつりはなりたたない。

materials.prompt: 〜抜く
materials.answer:
to do all the way through; to see through to the end (despite hardship)

〜抜く attaches to the ます-stem and says an action was carried all the way to the end, usually against difficulty — 走り抜く = run all the way through, 考え抜く = think something through completely, やり抜く = see it through to the finish. The nuance is persistence and endurance, not mere completion. It conjugates as an う-verb (抜いた, 抜いて).
materials.reading: ぬく
materials.notes:
Attach it to the stem: やり抜く, not やる抜く.

〜抜く stresses enduring through hardship to the finish, while 〜切る stresses using something up or reaching a clean end — 戦い抜く (fight all the way through) vs 使い切る (use it all up).

Synonyms: kiru — 〜切る also means 'do thoroughly / completely'; 抜く emphasizes persevering through hardship, 切る emphasizes finishing off entirely.

Synonyms: toosu — 〜通す means 'keep doing all the way through'; 抜く adds the sense of pushing through difficulty to the end.

Related: owaru — 〜終わる neutrally marks finishing an action; 抜く adds the effort and endurance of reaching the end.

Source references: jlptsensei, bunpro

examples.japanese: どんなに苦しくても、最後まで走り抜くつもりだ。
examples.english: No matter how hard it gets, I intend to run all the way to the finish.
examples.reading: どんなにくるしくても、さいごまではしりぬくつもりだ。

examples.japanese: 悩み抜いた末に、彼女は会社を辞める決心をした。
examples.english: After agonizing over it thoroughly, she made up her mind to quit the company.
examples.reading: なやみぬいたすえに、かのじょはかいしゃをやめるけっしんをした。

materials.prompt: を中心に
materials.answer:
centered on; with ~ at the center; mainly among ~

を中心に（して） marks the thing that sits at the center of some activity, group, or arrangement — everything else gathers around it or is organized with it as the focus. 駅を中心に = centered on the station; 若者を中心に = mainly among young people.
materials.reading: をちゅうしんに
materials.notes:
を中心に marks the focal point that other things arrange themselves around; it isn't a plain 'about (a topic)' — for simply discussing a subject, use について.

bunpro lists N2

Related: o-megutte — をめぐって centers a dispute or discussion around an issue; を中心に marks a focal point things are arranged around, without the sense of contention.

Related: ni-tsuite — について marks the topic you talk or think about; を中心に marks what sits at the center of an activity or group.

Source references: jlptsensei, bunpro
structures: Noun ＋ を中心とした ＋ Noun

examples.japanese: この町では、駅を中心に店が並んでいます。
examples.english: In this town, the shops are lined up centered around the station.
examples.reading: このまちでは、えきをちゅうしんにみせがならんでいます。

examples.japanese: その歌手は若い人を中心に人気があります。
examples.english: That singer is popular mainly among young people.
examples.reading: そのかしゅはわかいひとをちゅうしんににんきがあります。

materials.prompt: 〜を踏まえて
materials.answer:
based on; taking ~ into account

〜を踏まえて means taking established facts, results, or opinions as the grounds for the next judgment or action: 現状を踏まえて対策を立てる = draw up measures taking the current situation into account; 前回の反省を踏まえて = building on the lessons of last time. 踏まえる means 'to base oneself on', so the reference is something already known and considered, not a future hypothetical. It is formal and common in discussion and policy.
materials.reading: をふまえて
materials.notes:
Take X (facts, results, opinions already established) as the basis for a judgment or action — not a future assumption (compare を前提に).

Formal register; typical objects are 現状・結果・意見・事実, things already on the table.

Synonyms: o-moto-ni — をもとに uses X as source material to produce something; を踏まえて takes X into consideration as grounds for a judgment.

Related: o-zentei-toshite — を前提に assumes a condition as given going forward; を踏まえて builds on facts already established.

Source references: jlptsensei, bunpro

examples.japanese: 前回の反省を踏まえて、今年は計画を大幅に見直した。
examples.english: Taking the lessons of last time into account, this year we substantially revised the plan.
examples.reading: ぜんかいのはんせいをふまえて、ことしはけいかくをおおはばにみなおした。

examples.japanese: 調査結果を踏まえて、今後の方針を決定する予定だ。
examples.english: We plan to decide our future policy on the basis of the survey results.
examples.reading: ちょうさけっかをふまえて、こんごのほうしんをけっていするよていだ。

materials.prompt: お・ご
materials.answer:
honorific prefixes お / ご

お and ご are polite prefixes placed on the front of nouns (and some adjectives) to make speech sound more refined or to show respect toward the listener or the thing's owner. As a rough rule, お joins native Japanese words (お金, お花) and ご joins words of Chinese origin (ご家族, ご住所). Some very common Chinese-origin words take お anyway by convention (お茶, お電話), so treat this as a starting guideline, not a strict rule.
materials.reading: お・ご
materials.notes:
As a guideline お joins native (訓読み) words and ご joins Sino-Japanese (音読み) words, but there are common exceptions — お茶, お電話, お時間 all take お even though the noun is Chinese-origin — so learn set phrases as you meet them.

Adding お/ご to your own things can sound like you are honoring yourself; for the listener's family say ご家族, but your own is just 家族.

Related: o-suru — お＋stem＋する is a humble verb pattern that reuses the same お prefix.

Related: o-kudasai-honorific — お＋stem＋ください makes a polite request using the same お prefix.

Related: gozaimasu — ございます is the polite existence verb often paired with お/ご speech.

Source references: jlptsensei

examples.japanese: お茶をどうぞ。
examples.english: Please have some tea.
examples.reading: おちゃをどうぞ。

examples.japanese: ご家族はお元気ですか。
examples.english: Is your family well?
examples.reading: ごかぞくはおげんきですか。

materials.prompt: をはじめ
materials.answer:
starting with ~; ~ and others like it; headed by ~

をはじめ（として） singles out one representative, usually the most prominent, member of a group and implies a wider set follows it — X and others like it. 東京をはじめ、大都市では… = In big cities, starting with Tokyo… The named item heads a list that isn't spelled out in full.
materials.reading: をはじめ
materials.notes:
The noun before をはじめ is the leading, most representative member of a group, not just a random example; it heads the list rather than being tucked into it.

Synonyms: nado — など lists an item as one example among others ('and so on'); をはじめ presents its noun as the leading member the rest follow.

Related: toka-toka — とか〜とか lists a couple of casual examples side by side; をはじめ names one prominent member standing in for a larger group.

Source references: jlptsensei, bunpro
structures: Noun ＋ をはじめとする ＋ Noun

examples.japanese: この店では、りんごをはじめ、いろいろな果物を売っています。
examples.english: This shop sells all kinds of fruit, starting with apples.
examples.reading: このみせでは、りんごをはじめ、いろいろなくだものをうっています。

examples.japanese: 校長先生をはじめ、多くの先生が卒業式に出席しました。
examples.english: Many teachers, headed by the principal, attended the graduation ceremony.
examples.reading: こうちょうせんせいをはじめ、おおくのせんせいがそつぎょうしきにしゅっせきしました。

materials.prompt: 〜を経て
materials.answer:
via; through; after (a process or interval)

〜を経て marks passing through a stage, place, or span of time on the way to a result: 長い交渉を経て合意に達した = reached agreement after long negotiations; パリを経てロンドンへ = via Paris to London. 経て is the て-form of 経る 'to pass through'. It is formal and written, emphasizing the intervening process that led to the final state.
materials.reading: をへて
materials.notes:
Formal and written; marks passing through a stage, place, or period of time on the way to an outcome.

経て is from 経る 'pass through', not 経つ 'time elapses' — the point is the process one goes through.

Synonyms: o-tsuujite — を通じて = by means of, or throughout a span; を経て = after passing through a stage on the way to a result.

Related: sue-ni — た末に stresses a final outcome after much effort/trouble; を経て neutrally marks the process or stages passed through.

Source references: jlptsensei, bunpro

examples.english: After a long discussion, we finally reached a conclusion everyone could accept.
examples.reading: ながいぎろんをへて、ようやくぜんいんがなっとくできるけつろんにたっした。

examples.english: Through countless hardships, he built up the position he holds today.
examples.reading: かれはいくたのこんなんをへて、いまのちいをきずきあげた。

materials.prompt: 〜を控えて
materials.answer:
with ~ close ahead; on the eve of

〜を控えて describes a situation in which an important event is imminent, and the main clause tells what is happening in the run-up: 試験を控えて猛勉強する = cram with exams looming; 出発を明日に控えて = with departure the next day. Here 控える means 'have (something) close ahead', temporally (or sometimes spatially). The impending event is usually significant, which colors the preparation or mood.
materials.reading: をひかえて
materials.notes:
This 控える means 'have (an event) looming close ahead', not the other sense of 控える 'to refrain from / hold back'.

The event is imminent and usually important; the main clause describes the situation or preparations leading up to it.

Related: ni-sakidachi — に先立ち = doing something in advance of an event; を控えて = being in the run-up with the event looming ahead.

Related: ni-atatte — にあたって marks the occasion of doing something; を控えて sets the scene of an imminent event and what happens before it.

Source references: jlptsensei

examples.japanese: 受験を間近に控えて、彼は毎日遅くまで勉強している。
examples.english: With the entrance exams close at hand, he studies late every day.
examples.reading: じゅけんをまぢかにひかえて、かれはまいにちおそくまでべんきょうしている。

examples.japanese: 開店を翌日に控えて、店内は準備に追われていた。
examples.english: With the opening the very next day, the shop was rushed off its feet with preparations.
examples.reading: かいてんをよくじつにひかえて、てんないはじゅんびにおわれていた。

materials.prompt: 〜をいいことに
materials.answer:
taking advantage of; exploiting (a favorable situation)

〜をいいことに marks a favorable circumstance that someone exploits to do something they arguably shouldn't. It carries clear criticism: 親が留守なのをいいことに = taking advantage of the parents being out. A noun takes を directly; a clause is nominalized with の first (いないのをいいことに). The speaker disapproves of the person for seizing on the situation.
materials.reading: をいいことに
materials.notes:
Almost always critical — the speaker blames someone for exploiting a situation, so it doesn't fit neutral 'given the chance' contexts.

After a clause, insert の before をいいことに: 先生がいないのをいいことに.

Related: o-yoso-ni — をよそに means acting in disregard of others' concerns; をいいことに means actively exploiting a convenient situation for one's own ends.

Source references: jlptsensei, bunpro

examples.english: Taking advantage of the teacher's absence, he started making a racket in the classroom.
examples.reading: かれはせんせいがいないのをいいことに、きょうしつでさわぎはじめた。

examples.japanese: 客が少ないのをいいことに、店員はずっとおしゃべりしていた。
examples.english: Taking advantage of there being few customers, the clerk chatted the entire time.
examples.reading: きゃくがすくないのをいいことに、てんいんはずっとおしゃべりしていた。

materials.prompt: 〜を顧みず・〜も顧みず
materials.answer:
without regard for; heedless of

〜を顧みず means acting without giving thought to something one arguably should heed — danger, one's own body, or one's family. 危険を顧みず火の中へ = plunging into the fire heedless of danger; 家庭を顧みない = neglectful of one's family. 顧みる literally means 'to look back on / pay heed to', so 顧みず is 'without heeding'. It is formal and largely written, and the も variant adds a 'not even' shading (身の危険も顧みず).
materials.reading: をかえりみず・もかえりみず
materials.notes:
Formal and written in register; the object is usually danger, one's own body/family, or consequences one would normally take into account.

顧みず is literary 'without looking back on / heeding' — not the same as merely 'not seeing'.

Synonyms: o-mono-tomo-sezu-ni — をものともせずに praises bravely overcoming a hardship; を顧みず emphasizes simply not giving thought to what one should heed.

Related: mo-kamawazu — もかまわず = not minding/caring about something; を顧みず specifically frames it as failing to give due heed to danger or one's own welfare.

Source references: jlptsensei, bunpro

examples.japanese: 消防士たちは危険を顧みず、炎の中へ飛び込んでいった。
examples.english: The firefighters plunged into the flames heedless of the danger.
examples.reading: しょうぼうしたちはきけんをかえりみず、ほのおのなかへとびこんでいった。

examples.japanese: 彼は自分の体も顧みず、夜遅くまで働き続けた。
examples.english: Without any regard even for his own health, he kept working late into the night.
examples.reading: かれはじぶんのからだもかえりみず、よるおそくまではたらきつづけた。

materials.prompt: 〜を限りに
materials.answer:
as of (the end of); ~ being the last

〜を限りに takes a time point or occasion as the final cutoff, after which something stops or changes for good: 今日を限りに = as of today; 本日を限りに閉店 = closing as of today. The following clause typically states an ending — a retirement, a shop's last day, quitting a habit. (A separate fixed idiom 声を限りに / 力の限り means 'to the utmost' and is unrelated to this time-cutoff use.)
materials.reading: をかぎりに
materials.notes:
Marks a time point as the last one, after which something ends; the main clause is normally an ending or cessation.

Don't confuse it with the fixed phrase 声を限りに ('at the top of one's voice'), which is 'to the utmost', not a time cutoff.

Synonyms: o-motte — をもって is a neutral formal 'as of / with (this)'; を限りに adds the feeling that this is the final time, the last.

Related: o-sakai-ni — を境に marks a dividing line with a before/after change; を限りに marks a final endpoint after which something simply stops.

Source references: jlptsensei, bunpro

examples.japanese: 今シーズンを限りに、彼は現役を引退することを発表した。
examples.english: He announced that he would retire from active play as of the end of this season.
examples.reading: こんシーズンをかぎりに、かれはげんえきをいんたいすることをはっぴょうした。

examples.japanese: 本日を限りに、この店は五十年の歴史に幕を下ろす。
examples.english: As of today, this shop brings the curtain down on its fifty years of history.
examples.reading: ほんじつをかぎりに、このみせはごじゅうねんのれきしにまくをおろす。

materials.prompt: 〜を兼ねて
materials.answer:
doubling as; also serving the purpose of

〜を兼ねて names a secondary purpose that a single action also fulfills. 運動を兼ねて歩く = walk, which also serves as exercise; 挨拶を兼ねて訪ねる = visit, partly to pay one's respects. The noun before を兼ねて is the additional aim; the main clause states the primary action that happens to cover it too. It comes from 兼ねる 'to combine two roles'.
materials.reading: をかねて
materials.notes:
The noun before を兼ねて is the secondary purpose; the main clause is the primary action that also fulfills it.

Both purposes are real and compatible — it's one act serving two ends, not choosing one over the other.

Source references: jlptsensei, bunpro

examples.english: To get some exercise as well, I try to commute by bicycle whenever I can.

examples.english: I went back to my hometown for the first time in ages, which also served as a reunion with old friends.
examples.reading: きゅうゆうとのさいかいをかねて、ひさしぶりにこきょうへかえった。

materials.prompt: 〜を皮切りに
materials.answer:
starting with; as the first of an unfolding series

〜を皮切りに marks X as the first instance from which a series spreads or expands — 東京公演を皮切りに全国ツアーが始まった = starting with the Tokyo show, a nationwide tour began. 皮切り literally means 'the first cut', and the following clause must describe a chain of events or a spreading development that grows out of that opening, not a single isolated act. It is formal and often used of tours, movements, and cascading reactions.
materials.reading: をかわきりに
materials.notes:
What follows must be a series or spreading development that grows from the first instance — not a single, unconnected event.

The named event is genuinely the chronological start of the chain, giving it a sense of momentum picking up.

Synonyms: o-hajime — をはじめ lists X as a representative example among others; を皮切りに marks X as the chronological first of a series that unfolds from it.

Source references: jlptsensei, bunpro
structures: Noun［first event］＋を皮切りに（して）／を皮切りとして

examples.japanese: 東京公演を皮切りに、全国各地でのツアーが始まった。
examples.english: Starting with the Tokyo performance, a tour across the country got under way.
examples.reading: とうきょうこうえんをかわきりに、ぜんこくかくちでのツアーがはじまった。

examples.japanese: 彼の勇気ある発言を皮切りに、次々と改革を求める声が上がり始めた。
examples.english: Beginning with his courageous remark, calls for reform began to rise one after another.
examples.reading: かれのゆうきあるはつげんをかわきりに、つぎつぎとかいかくをもとめるこえがあがりはじめた。

materials.prompt: を契機に
materials.answer:
as a turning point; taking ... as the opportunity

を契機に(して) / を契機として marks an event as the turning point or catalyst that prompts a significant change or new direction — 'taking X as the occasion, using X as a turning point'. It is formal and written, and tends to accompany weighty, large-scale developments.
materials.reading: をけいきに
materials.notes:
It is formal and written; for small everyday triggers, をきっかけに sounds more natural.

It usually introduces notable, large changes (reforms, life decisions) rather than trivial shifts.

Synonyms: o-kikkake-ni — をきっかけに carries the same 'trigger' sense but is more everyday; を契機に is heavier and more formal.

Source references: jlptsensei, bunpro

examples.japanese: 定年退職を契機に、彼は長年の夢だった世界一周の旅に出た。
examples.english: Taking his retirement as a turning point, he set off on the round-the-world journey he had long dreamed of.
examples.reading: ていねんたいしょくをけいきに、かれはながねんのゆめだったせかいいっしゅうのたびにでた。

examples.japanese: この事故を契機として、会社は安全管理を全面的に見直した。
examples.english: Prompted by this accident, the company thoroughly overhauled its safety management.
examples.reading: このじこをけいきとして、かいしゃはあんぜんかんりをぜんめんてきにみなおした。

materials.prompt: 〜を機に
materials.answer:
taking ~ as the occasion/opportunity (for a change)

〜を機に treats an event as the occasion that prompts a deliberate new action or change: 結婚を機に転職した = took marriage as the occasion to change jobs; 定年を機に = on the occasion of retirement. It is fairly formal, and the following clause is a chosen action, not an automatic consequence. 機 here is 'opportunity/turning point'.
materials.reading: をきに
materials.notes:
The following clause is a deliberate action or change taken because of the event, not a spontaneous result.

Fairly formal; for everyday speech, をきっかけに feels more casual.

Synonyms: o-keiki-ni — を契機に is near-identical in meaning and slightly more formal/literary; を機に is the shorter everyday equivalent.

Synonyms: o-kikkake-ni — をきっかけに is the more colloquial 'triggered by'; を機に is more formal and leans toward a chosen life change.

Related: o-sakai-ni — を境に stresses a before/after dividing line; を機に stresses seizing the event as an opportunity to act.

Source references: jlptsensei, bunpro

examples.japanese: 定年を機に、夫婦で田舎に移り住むことにした。
examples.english: Taking his retirement as the occasion, the couple decided to move to the countryside.
examples.reading: ていねんをきに、ふうふでいなかにうつりすむことにした。

examples.japanese: 今回の失敗を機に、業務の進め方を一から見直すことにした。
examples.english: Using this failure as a turning point, we decided to review our workflow from scratch.
examples.reading: こんかいのしっぱいをきに、ぎょうむのすすめかたをいちからみなおすことにした。

materials.prompt: をきっかけに・がきっかけで
materials.answer:
with ... as the trigger; taking ... as the start

をきっかけに(して) / がきっかけで marks an event as the trigger or occasion that set off a change, a new habit, or a development — 'taking X as the trigger, ever since X'. It is neutral about whether the result is good or bad, and belongs to everyday as well as written Japanese.
materials.reading: をきっかけに・がきっかけで
materials.notes:
がきっかけで foregrounds X as the cause, while をきっかけに frames X as something taken up as a starting point.

It marks the trigger of a change; the following clause should describe the new development that resulted.

Synonyms: o-keiki-ni — を契機に is the more formal, written near-synonym; をきっかけに suits everyday triggers and small changes too.

Source references: jlptsensei, bunpro
structures: Noun ＋ をきっかけに（して）

examples.japanese: 入院をきっかけに、彼は食生活を見直すようになった。
examples.english: His hospital stay was the trigger for him to start rethinking his diet.
examples.reading: にゅういんをきっかけに、かれはしょくせいかつをみなおすようになった。

examples.japanese: ある本との出会いがきっかけで、彼女は作家を目指し始めた。
examples.english: An encounter with a certain book was the trigger, and she began aiming to become a writer.
examples.reading: あるほんとのであいがきっかけで、かのじょはさっかをめざしはじめた。

materials.prompt: 〜を禁じ得ない
materials.answer:
cannot suppress (an emotion); can't help feeling

〜を禁じ得ない takes an emotion noun and says one cannot forbid it welling up: 涙を禁じ得ない = can't hold back tears; 怒りを禁じ得ない = can't suppress anger. 禁じ得ない literally means 'cannot forbid (in oneself)'. It is distinctly formal, appearing in written and formal-spoken contexts, and describes a feeling that arises naturally in the speaker or as a general human reaction.
materials.reading: をきんじえない
materials.notes:
The object is an emotion noun (涙・怒り・驚き・同情), not an action — you can't say 行くのを禁じ得ない.

Formal register; describes an emotion welling up in oneself, so it isn't used to report someone else's feelings casually.

Synonyms: zaru-o-enai — ざるを得ない = have no choice but to (do an action); を禁じ得ない = cannot suppress (an emotion) — different objects.

Related: ni-taeru-ni-taenai — 〜に堪えない (感慨に堪えない) also expresses an overwhelming feeling; を禁じ得ない specifically frames it as an emotion one cannot hold back.

Source references: jlptsensei, bunpro

examples.japanese: あまりに理不尽な仕打ちに、怒りを禁じ得なかった。
examples.english: Faced with such an unreasonable act, I could not suppress my anger.
examples.reading: あまりにりふじんなしうちに、いかりをきんじえなかった。

examples.japanese: 被災地の惨状を目にして、涙を禁じ得なかった。
examples.english: Seeing the devastation in the disaster area, I could not hold back my tears.
examples.reading: ひさいちのさんじょうをめにして、なみだをきんじえなかった。

materials.prompt: を込めて
materials.answer:
putting (feeling or effort) into; filled with ~

を込めて attaches to a noun naming a feeling or energy and says the following action is carried out with that feeling poured into it — 心を込めて = with all one's heart, 感謝を込めて = with gratitude. The noun names the emotion or effort that fills the act.
materials.reading: をこめて
materials.notes:
The noun names a feeling or energy put into the act (心, 愛, 感謝, 願い); it is not used for physically filling a container with something.

Don't mix it up with だらけ ('covered in / full of'), which describes a surface littered with something unwanted; を込めて is about pouring emotion into an action, even though both can be glossed 'full of'.

bunpro lists N2

Related: darake — 〜だらけ means a surface is covered in or full of something (usually unwanted); を込めて is about putting feeling into an action.

Source references: jlptsensei, bunpro

examples.japanese: 母に感謝を込めて手紙を書きました。
examples.english: I wrote a letter to my mother with heartfelt gratitude.
examples.reading: ははにかんしゃをこめててがみをかきました。

examples.japanese: 彼女は心を込めて歌を歌った。
examples.english: She sang the song with all her heart.
examples.reading: かのじょはこころをこめてうたをうたった。

materials.prompt: お～ください
materials.answer:
please do ~ (honorific request)

お＋verb stem＋ください is a polished, honorific way to ask someone to do something — the kind of request you hear in shops and announcements. お待ちください = please wait; ご利用ください = please use. It is more respectful than the everyday 〜てください.
materials.notes:
No する or して goes in the middle: it is お待ちください, not お待ちしてください.

する-verbs of Chinese origin usually take ご, not お: ご記入ください, ご注意ください.

Synonyms: te-kudasai — 〜てください is the plain polite request; お～ください is the more honorific, formal version.

Related: o-ni-naru — お～になる describes a respected person's action; お～ください asks them to perform one.

Related: nasai — なさい is a firm command from a superior downward; お～ください is a respectful upward request.

Source references: jlptsensei, bunpro
structures: ご ＋ Noun［する-verb］ ＋ ください

examples.japanese: 少々お待ちください。
examples.english: Please wait a moment.
examples.reading: しょうしょうおまちください。

examples.japanese: エレベーターをご利用ください。
examples.english: Please use the elevator.
examples.reading: エレベーターをごりようください。

materials.prompt: をめぐって
materials.answer:
concerning; over (a matter of dispute)

をめぐって / をめぐる marks the central issue that people argue, debate, compete, or hold conflicting views about — 'over, concerning, surrounding'. It typically introduces a matter of contention involving several parties. Use をめぐる when modifying a following noun (をめぐる議論).
materials.reading: をめぐって
materials.notes:
It implies multiple parties in disagreement or discussion around the topic, unlike the neutral 'about' of について.

Before a noun, switch to the form をめぐる: をめぐる論争, not をめぐって論争.

Synonyms: ni-tsuite — について is a neutral 'about / concerning' with no conflict implied; をめぐって suggests contention among parties.

Related: ni-oite — において marks a domain or setting ('in, regarding'); をめぐって marks the specific issue people are at odds over.

Source references: jlptsensei, bunpro

examples.japanese: その土地の所有権をめぐって、二つの家族が長く争ってきた。
examples.english: Two families have long been in dispute over the ownership of that land.
examples.reading: そのとちのしょゆうけんをめぐって、ふたつのかぞくがながくあらそってきた。

examples.japanese: 新しい法案をめぐる議論が、国会で続いている。
examples.english: Debate over the new bill continues in the Diet.
examples.reading: あたらしいほうあんをめぐるぎろんが、こっかいでつづいている。

materials.prompt: 〜をものともせずに
materials.answer:
undaunted by; in defiance of (a hardship or danger)

〜をものともせず（に） attaches to a noun naming a difficulty, danger, or setback and says the subject pressed on without being cowed by it — 困難をものともせず (undaunted by hardship), 荒波をものともせず (in defiance of the rough seas). The tone is admiring: it praises someone for bravely facing down an obstacle, so it usually describes other people's courage rather than one's own trivial troubles.
materials.reading: をものともせずに
materials.notes:
The noun must be a real hardship or danger that the subject overcomes admirably; it does not fit petty inconveniences.

The nuance is praise for bravery, so it is normally used of others, not to describe your own everyday situation.

せず is the classical negative of する; there is no をものともしずに.

Synonyms: nimo-kakawarazu — にもかかわらず neutrally states 'despite'; をものともせず adds that the subject bravely overpowered the obstacle.

Related: o-yoso-ni — をよそに also means acting in the face of something, but coolly disregards concern one ought to heed; をものともせず courageously overcomes a hardship.

Source references: jlptsensei, bunpro

examples.japanese: 彼女は度重なる失敗をものともせず、研究を続けた。
examples.english: Undaunted by one failure after another, she carried on with her research.
examples.reading: かのじょはたびかさなるしっぱいをものともせず、けんきゅうをつづけた。

examples.japanese: 選手たちは悪天候をものともせずに、試合を最後まで戦い抜いた。
examples.english: In defiance of the terrible weather, the players fought the match out to the very end.
examples.reading: せんしゅたちはあくてんこうをものともせずに、しあいをさいごまでたたかいぬいた。

materials.prompt: をもとに
materials.answer:
based on; on the basis of; drawing on

をもとに(して) / をもとにした marks the material, source, or reference used to create or judge something — 'based on, drawing on'. The following action builds on that source as its foundation: 事件をもとに作った映画 = 'a film made based on the incident'. Use をもとにした before a noun.
materials.reading: をもとに
materials.notes:
The source is raw material you build or judge from (data, a story, experience), so the following clause is usually one of creating or evaluating.

Compare に基づいて, which stresses conforming to a rule or principle; をもとに stresses using something as source material.

Synonyms: ni-motozuite — に基づいて also means 'based on', but emphasizes acting in accordance with a rule or principle rather than using source material.

Source references: jlptsensei, bunpro
structures: Noun ＋ をもとにした ＋ Noun

examples.japanese: この映画は、実際に起きた事件をもとに作られたそうだ。
examples.english: This film was apparently made based on an incident that really happened.
examples.reading: このえいがは、じっさいにおきたじけんをもとにつくられたそうだ。

examples.japanese: アンケートの結果をもとに、新商品の改良を進めた。
examples.english: Drawing on the survey results, we went ahead with improvements to the new product.
examples.reading: アンケートのけっかをもとに、しんしょうひんのかいりょうをすすめた。

materials.prompt: 〜をもって・〜をもちまして
materials.answer:
with; by means of; as of (a set time or point)

〜をもって attaches to a noun in two formal senses. As 'by means of / with' it names the means, standard, or quality through which something is done — 誠意をもって対応する (deal with it in good faith), 書面をもって通知する (notify in writing). As 'as of / effective from' it marks a fixed point that draws a line — 本日をもって (as of today), 五時をもって (as of five o'clock) — after which a state ends or begins. をもちまして is the politer form heard in announcements and ceremonies. Both belong to written and formal spoken register, not casual で.
materials.reading: をもって・をもちまして
materials.notes:
Two distinct senses: 'by means of / with' (naming a method or quality) and 'as of / effective from' (a fixed cut-off point). Context tells them apart.

This is formal and written; in everyday speech で ('by means of') is normal, not をもって.

をもちまして is a politeness variant used in announcements, not a separate meaning.

Synonyms: nite — にて is a formal で for means or place; をもって in its 'by means of' sense is even more formal and often names a quality or standard.

Related: o-kagiri-ni — を限りに also sets a final cut-off point in time, but stresses that something ends there; をもって can mark either an ending or a starting boundary.

Source references: jlptsensei, bunpro
structures: Noun［point in time］＋をもって／をもちまして

examples.japanese: 当店は本日をもちまして閉店させていただきます。
examples.english: As of today, our store will be closing for good.
examples.reading: とうてんはほんじつをもちましてへいてんさせていただきます。

examples.japanese: 選考の結果は、後日書面をもってお知らせいたします。
examples.english: The results of the selection will be communicated to you in writing at a later date.
examples.reading: せんこうのけっかは、ごじつしょめんをもっておしらせいたします。

materials.prompt: お〜願う
materials.answer:
to (humbly) request that you ~; we ask you to ~

お＋a verb stem＋願う (or ご＋a Sino-Japanese noun＋願う) forms a very polite, businesslike request that the listener do something — お待ち願います = I ask that you wait, ご了承願います = I ask for your understanding. It is common in announcements, notices, and formal correspondence. The request is directed at the listener's action and is normally used in the 願います / 願いたい form.
materials.notes:
Keep it polite (願います / 願いたく), as bare 願う can sound blunt.

Use ご with Sino-Japanese nouns (ご確認願います) and お with native verb stems (お待ち願います).

Related: o-suru — お〜する humbles the speaker's OWN action; お〜願う asks the LISTENER to perform an action.

Related: te-kudasai — てください is a plainer polite request; お〜願う is more formal and typical of notices and business settings.

Source references: jlptsensei, bunpro

examples.english: Should there be any points that are unclear, please make an inquiry.
examples.reading: ごふめいなてんがございましたら、おといあわせねがいます。

examples.japanese: 危険ですので、白線の内側までお下がり願います。
examples.english: As it is dangerous, we ask you to step back behind the white line.
examples.reading: きけんですので、はくせんのうちがわまでおさがりねがいます。

materials.prompt: お～になる
materials.answer:
to do ~ (honorific)

お＋verb stem＋になる is the general honorific (sonkeigo) pattern for a respected person's action. お帰りになる = (they) go home; お書きになる = (they) write. It raises the subject, so you use it about a customer, boss or teacher — not about yourself.
materials.notes:
It is honorific: it describes someone else's action. For your own action use the humble お～する.

Some verbs use a special honorific word instead of this pattern: 見る → ご覧になる, not お見になる.

Antonyms: o-suru — お～する humbly lowers your own action; お～になる honorifically raises someone else's.

Related: irassharu — いらっしゃる is a ready-made honorific verb; お～になる turns ordinary verbs honorific.

Related: o-kudasai-honorific — お～ください requests an action; お～になる simply describes a respected person doing it.

Source references: jlptsensei, bunpro
structures: ご ＋ Noun［する-verb］ ＋ になる

examples.english: The president has already left for home.

examples.english: Did you read this book, sensei?
examples.reading: せんせいはこのほんをおよみになりましたか。

materials.prompt: を除いて
materials.answer:
except for; excluding; apart from

を除いて / を除き sets one item aside from an otherwise general statement — 'except for, excluding, apart from'. What follows is presented as true for everything but the excepted thing: 日曜を除いて毎日 = 'every day except Sunday'.
materials.reading: をのぞいて
materials.notes:
を除き is the more formal, written form of を除いて.

It carves out a specific exception from a general claim; compare 以外, which is a more neutral, everyday 'other than'.

Synonyms: igai — 以外 ('other than') is the everyday, neutral counterpart; を除いて more explicitly frames an item as an exception being removed.

Source references: jlptsensei, bunpro

examples.japanese: 日曜を除いて、この図書館は毎日利用できます。
examples.english: This library can be used every day except Sunday.
examples.reading: にちようをのぞいて、このとしょかんはまいにちりようできます。

examples.japanese: 一部の地域を除き、明日は全国的に晴れるでしょう。
examples.english: Except for some areas, it will be sunny nationwide tomorrow.
examples.reading: いちぶのちいきをのぞき、あしたはぜんこくてきにはれるでしょう。

materials.prompt: 〜をおいて〜ない
materials.answer:
no one/nothing but; none other than

〜をおいて〜ない singles out X as the one and only option, ending in a negative: 彼をおいて適任者はいない = there is no one suited but him. The をおいて here means 'setting aside / other than', and ほかに is often inserted (をおいてほかにない). It carries strong positive evaluation, presenting X as uniquely qualified with no real alternative.
materials.notes:
The sentence must close in a negative (いない／ない); it singles out X as the sole choice, usually with praise.

This おいて is 'other than / apart from', not the verb 置いて 'placing (something)'.

Synonyms: o-nozoite — を除いて simply excludes X from a set; をおいて〜ない goes further, saying X is the sole option and nothing else qualifies.

Related: nara-dewa — ならでは also stresses uniqueness ('only X can'), but as a positive attribute of X; をおいて〜ない frames it through a negation of all alternatives.

Source references: jlptsensei, bunpro

examples.reading: かいしゃをたてなおせるじんぶつは、あのひとをおいてかんがえられない。

materials.prompt: 〜を押して・〜を押し切って
materials.answer:
doing something despite opposition or one's own poor condition

〜を押して and 〜を押し切って mean forging ahead despite an obstacle. を押し切って stresses forcibly overriding others' resistance — 周囲の反対を押し切って結婚した = married in the face of everyone's objections. を押して is often used of acting despite one's own condition — 病を押して出席する = attend despite illness. The object is the obstacle being overcome (opposition, illness), not a physical thing.
materials.reading: をおして・をおしきって
materials.notes:
を押し切って = force one's way past others' opposition; を押して is typically used of pressing on despite one's own poor condition (熱を押して).

The object is the obstacle (反対・病気), not a literal object; 押す here is figurative 'push through', not physical pushing.

Related: o-mono-tomo-sezu-ni — をものともせずに = undaunted by hardship, admiring the resolve; を押し切って highlights the act of forcibly overriding resistance.

Related: o-kaerimizu — を顧みず = without giving thought to danger/consequences; を押して = pressing on despite an obstacle one is clearly aware of.

Source references: jlptsensei

examples.reading: しゅういのはんたいをおしきって、かれはきぎょうするみちをえらんだ。

examples.english: Pushing through a high fever, she stayed on stage right to the end.

materials.prompt: 〜を境に
materials.answer:
with ~ as the dividing line/turning point

〜を境に takes a time point or event as a boundary and marks a clear before/after contrast: あの日を境に彼は変わった = from that day on, as a dividing line, he changed. 境 means 'boundary', so the emphasis is on how noticeably different things are on either side of that point. It often pairs with life-changing events, ages, or seasons.
materials.reading: をさかいに
materials.notes:
The emphasis is on a marked before/after contrast around the boundary — not merely that something happened at that time.

Compare を機に, which stresses seizing an occasion to act; を境に stresses the dividing line itself.

Synonyms: o-ki-ni — を機に seizes an event as an opportunity for a chosen action; を境に marks a boundary with a clear before/after change.

Related: o-kagiri-ni — を限りに marks a final endpoint after which something stops; を境に marks a point where things change from one state to another.

Source references: jlptsensei, bunpro
structures: Noun［time／event］＋を境に（して）／を境として

examples.japanese: 大病を境に、彼は生き方をすっかり変えた。
examples.english: A serious illness marked a turning point, and he completely changed the way he lived.
examples.reading: たいびょうをさかいに、かれはいきかたをすっかりかえた。

examples.english: Around the age of thirty, as a dividing line, I began to feel my strength declining.
examples.reading: さんじゅうさいをさかいに、たいりょくのおとろえをかんじるようになった。

materials.prompt: お～する
materials.answer:
to (humbly) do ~ for someone

お＋verb stem＋する is the humble (kenjougo) pattern for your own action when it touches someone you respect. お持ちします = I'll carry it (for you); お送りします = I'll see you off. It lowers you to raise the other person. する-verbs of Chinese origin take ご instead: ご案内する.
materials.notes:
It is humble, so the doer is you or your group — never use it for the listener's action (that would be お～になる).

Use the verb stem, not the dictionary form: お持ちします, not お持つします.

Synonyms: itasu — お～いたす swaps する for the humble いたす — the same pattern, one step more formal.

Antonyms: o-ni-naru — お～になる raises the other person's action; お～する humbly lowers your own.

Related: o-kudasai-honorific — お～ください asks the listener to act; お～する is you acting humbly for them.

Source references: bunpro

materials.prompt: を問わず
materials.answer:
regardless of; irrespective of

を問わず attaches to a noun to say something applies without regard to that factor — 'regardless of, irrespective of'. It typically follows a noun naming a variable (年齢, 経験) or a pair of opposites (男女, 昼夜), and the statement then holds true across all of them. It is formal in tone.
materials.reading: をとわず
materials.notes:
It takes a noun (a category, variable, or pair of opposites), not a clause or a か-question.

It is formal and written; にかかわらず is broader in what it can attach to and slightly less formal.

Synonyms: ni-kakawarazu — にかかわらず also means 'regardless of' but attaches more freely, including to plain forms and か-questions.

Synonyms: ikan-ni-kakawarazu — いかんにかかわらず means 'regardless of what X is'; it is more formal and rigid than を問わず.

Source references: jlptsensei, bunpro

examples.english: This job welcomes motivated people regardless of experience.
examples.reading: このしごとはけいけんをとわず、やるきのあるひとをかんげいします。

examples.english: That cafe bustles with tourists regardless of the season.
examples.reading: そのカフェは、きせつをとわずおおくのかんこうきゃくでにぎわっている。

materials.prompt: を通じて・を通して
materials.answer:
through; by way of; throughout

を通じて / を通して marks a medium or intermediary that something passes through — a person, a channel, an experience — or a whole span of time or area over which something holds. 友達を通じて = through a friend; 一年を通して = all year round.
materials.reading: をつうじて・をとおして
materials.notes:
Two senses share the form: with a person or means it reads 'by way of', with a time span or area it reads 'throughout'; the noun tells you which.

を通して leans slightly toward actively using the means, を通じて slightly toward the result or the span, but they overlap and are often interchangeable.

bunpro lists N2

Synonyms: ni-yotte — によって marks the means or cause 'by which' something is done; を通じて marks a medium or intermediary the action passes through.

Related: ni-watatte — にわたって stresses the full extent of a range or period ('spanning'); を通じて in its time sense says something holds steadily throughout.

materials.prompt: 〜を余儀なくされる
materials.answer:
to be forced to; to have no choice but to (undergo)

〜を余儀なくされる is the passive side of the pair: the person or organization affected is the subject, and outside circumstances leave them no choice but to accept some outcome. The unwanted outcome is an action noun (欠場, 閉鎖, 延期) marked with を. けがで欠場を余儀なくされた = was forced to sit out because of injury. It stresses that the situation was imposed from without, and it belongs to formal, written register.
materials.reading: をよぎなくされる
materials.notes:
The affected person is the subject and the を-noun is what they are forced into; contrast 〜を余儀なくさせる, where the cause is the subject.

The を-noun is normally a する-type action noun such as 中止・閉鎖・延期.

It emphasizes that circumstances imposed the outcome, so it carries a sense of reluctance and belongs to formal writing.

Synonyms: zaru-o-enai — ざるを得ない attaches to a verb and voices personal, reluctant resignation; を余儀なくされる attaches to an action noun and stresses that external circumstances imposed it.

Synonyms: shikanai-no-choice — しかない plainly says 'there is nothing to do but'; を余儀なくされる is far more formal and frames the outcome as forced upon one from outside.

Related: o-yogi-naku-saseru — The causative counterpart: 〜を余儀なくさせる makes the cause the subject, while 〜を余儀なくされる makes the forced person the subject.

Source references: jlptsensei, bunpro

examples.reading: ぎょうせきのあっかにより、かいしゃはおおくのてんぽのへいさをよぎなくされた。

materials.prompt: 〜を余儀なくさせる
materials.answer:
to force (a situation); to make (something) unavoidable

〜を余儀なくさせる is the causative side of this pair: an impersonal cause — a circumstance, event, or condition — is the subject and forces some outcome to happen. The forced outcome is a noun of action (中止, 撤退, 変更) marked with を, and the person pushed into it takes に. 不況が事業の縮小を余儀なくさせた = the recession forced a scaling-back of the business. It is stiff, written register typical of news and reports.
materials.reading: をよぎなくさせる
materials.notes:
The subject is the impersonal cause that does the forcing; contrast 〜を余儀なくされる, where the affected person is the subject.

The を-noun is normally a する-type action noun such as 中止・変更・撤退, not a concrete object.

Register is formal and written; it rarely appears in casual conversation.

Related: o-yogi-naku-sareru — The passive counterpart: 〜を余儀なくされる puts the forced person in the subject slot, while 〜を余儀なくさせる puts the cause there.

Source references: bunpro

examples.english: A shortage of funds forced a sweeping revision of the plan.
examples.reading: しきんふそくが、けいかくのおおはばなみなおしをよぎなくさせた。

examples.reading: たいふうのせっきんは、しゅさいしゃにたいかいのちゅうしをよぎなくさせた。

materials.prompt: 〜をよそに
materials.answer:
disregarding; ignoring; without regard to

〜をよそに attaches to a noun — usually someone's worry, opposition, or concern — and says the subject went ahead as if it were none of their business. 親の心配をよそに (heedless of his parents' worry), 周囲の反対をよそに (ignoring everyone's objections). The nuance is often critical: the subject coolly brushes aside something they really ought to have taken into account. It is written and formal in flavor.
materials.reading: をよそに
materials.notes:
The ignored noun is typically other people's feelings, concern, or opposition, and the tone is frequently disapproving.

Do not confuse it with 〜をものともせず: をよそに coolly disregards what one should heed, while をものともせず bravely overcomes a hardship.

Related: o-mono-tomo-sezu-ni — をものともせず admiringly overcomes a hardship; をよそに coolly, often selfishly, disregards concern one ought to weigh.

Related: nimo-kakawarazu — にもかかわらず neutrally says 'despite the fact that'; をよそに specifically shrugs off others' feelings or objections.

Source references: jlptsensei, bunpro

examples.japanese: 親の心配をよそに、彼は危険な冒険の旅に出かけていった。
examples.english: Heedless of his parents' worry, he set off on a dangerous adventure.
examples.reading: おやのしんぱいをよそに、かれはきけんなぼうけんのたびにでかけていった。

examples.japanese: 住民の反対をよそに、工事は着々と進められた。
examples.english: Ignoring the residents' opposition, the construction pressed steadily ahead.
examples.reading: じゅうみんのはんたいをよそに、こうじはちゃくちゃくとすすめられた。

materials.prompt: 〜を前提として・〜を前提に
materials.answer:
on the premise/assumption of

〜を前提として / 〜を前提に marks something as a precondition assumed to hold before proceeding: 結婚を前提に付き合う = date with marriage as the premise; 予算の確保を前提とする = premised on securing the budget. A clause is nominalized with こと first (〜ことを前提に). It is formal, common in planning, agreements, and business, and states an assumed basis rather than a mere hope.
materials.reading: をぜんていとして・をぜんていに
materials.notes:
For a clause, nominalize first: 〜ことを前提に / 〜という前提で.

It states a precondition taken as given going forward — not a fact already established (compare を踏まえて).

Synonyms: o-fumaete — を踏まえて builds on facts already established; を前提に assumes a condition as given before moving ahead.

Related: o-moto-ni — をもとに uses X as source material for making something; を前提に treats X as a condition assumed to hold.

Source references: jlptsensei, bunpro

examples.english: They began dating seriously, with marriage as the premise.
examples.reading: かれらはけっこんをぜんていに、しんけんにこうさいをはじめた。

materials.prompt: おかげで
materials.answer:
thanks to; owing to; because of (a good result)

〜おかげで credits a cause with a good outcome — 'thanks to ~'. 先生のおかげで = thanks to my teacher, 天気が良かったおかげで = thanks to the good weather. The default tone is gratitude, so it normally pairs a cause with a welcome result.
materials.reading: おかげで
materials.notes:
〜おかげで normally credits a good result; for a bad result you blame on something, use 〜せいで.

It can be turned ironic ('thanks a lot…') for a bad outcome, but its plain meaning is genuine thanks.

Antonyms: sei-de — 〜せいで pins a bad result on a cause ('because of ~, unfortunately'); 〜おかげで credits a good result.

Related: tame-ni — 〜ために gives a neutral cause or purpose; 〜おかげで specifically thanks a cause for a good outcome.

Source references: jlptsensei, bunpro

examples.english: Thanks to the good weather, the trip was a lot of fun.
examples.reading: てんきがよかったおかげで、りょこうはとてもたのしかったです。

materials.prompt: おきに
materials.answer:
at intervals of; every other

おきに follows a number-plus-counter to say something repeats with that gap left in between. 10分おきに = every ten minutes; 1日おきに = every other day. The idea is the space you leave between one occurrence and the next.
materials.reading: おきに
materials.notes:
おきに names the gap left between times, so 1日おきに means every OTHER day (skipping a day), not every day. For 'every single day' use 1日ごとに.

It needs a counted interval in front of it; to say 'each (item)' generally, use ごとに or the prefix 各.

bunpro lists N3

Related: goto-ni — ごとに counts every unit (毎回); おきに counts the gaps between, giving 'every other'.

Related: kaku — 各 is a prefix meaning 'each ~' on a noun; おきに measures a repeating interval.

Source references: jlptsensei, bunpro

examples.japanese: 花に1日おきに水をやっています。
examples.english: I water the flowers every other day.

materials.prompt: おまけに
materials.answer:
on top of that; what's more; to make matters worse

おまけに is a conjunction that adds a further point piling onto what was just said — usually in the same direction, so a second bad thing on top of a bad one (or a second good thing on top of a good one). It often carries the flavor 'and to make matters worse'. It links whole statements, not nouns.
materials.reading: おまけに
materials.notes:
It adds a circumstance in the same direction, not a contrast; use しかし / でも to turn the point around.

It joins statements, so it stands at the head of the added clause, not between two nouns.

Synonyms: sono-ue — その上 also means 'on top of that'; おまけに is more colloquial and often tinged with 'to make things worse'.

Synonyms: shikamo — しかも is a more formal 'moreover'; おまけに sounds casual and everyday.

Related: sara-ni — さらに adds and intensifies ('furthermore, even more'); おまけに simply tacks on an extra circumstance.

Source references: jlptsensei, bunpro

examples.english: I've had a headache since this morning, and on top of that I've even started running a fever.
examples.reading: きょうはあさからあたまがいたくて、おまけにねつまででてきた。

examples.japanese: あの店は値段が安くて、おまけに料理もおいしい。
examples.english: That restaurant is cheap, and what's more the food is delicious too.
examples.reading: あのみせはねだんがやすくて、おまけにりょうりもおいしい。

materials.prompt: 〜思いをする
materials.answer:
to have a ~ experience; to feel ~ (an emotion) keenly

〜思いをする describes undergoing an experience colored by a particular feeling, with the feeling word placed before 思い. 悔しい思いをする = go through something galling; つらい思いをする = have a painful experience; 恥ずかしい思いをする = suffer embarrassment. It takes an い-adjective, or a な-adjective + な, before 思い and focuses on how an experience felt to the person.
materials.reading: おもいをする
materials.notes:
The adjective describes how the experience felt; 思いをする centers the subjective feeling, not a mere action.

materials.prompt: 思うように
materials.answer:
the way one wants/expects (very often used in the negative)

思うように means 'as one wishes / as one expects things to go'. In practice it appears most often with a negative verb — 思うようにいかない, 思うようにできない — to say that things are not going the way one had hoped, usually with a note of frustration.
materials.reading: おもうように
materials.notes:
It most naturally pairs with a negative verb (思うように進まない = it isn't going as I'd hoped); a plain affirmative is comparatively rare.

思うように describes whether things go as one wishes, so it usually implies effort against an obstacle rather than a neutral statement.

Synonyms: toori-ni — 通りに (as in 思った通り) also means 'as expected', but is neutral; 思うように leans toward whether things go as one wishes, often in the negative.

Source references: bunpro

materials.prompt: おおよそ
materials.answer:
roughly; approximately; in general

おおよそ is an adverb meaning 'roughly / approximately', giving an inexact figure or a broad outline — おおよそ二時間かかる = takes roughly two hours, おおよその見当がつく = get a rough idea. It can also mean 'generally / by and large'. It is slightly formal; およそ is the shorter, more common variant. It stands before the amount or statement it qualifies.
materials.reading: おおよそ
materials.notes:
おおよそ is an adverb placed before the amount (おおよそ十人); the suffix くらい follows the amount (十人くらい).

It gives an approximate whole and can also mean 'by and large / on the whole'.

Synonyms: kurai-gurai — くらい marks approximation as a suffix after a number (十人くらい); おおよそ is an adverb standing before it.

Source references: bunpro

materials.prompt: 〜折に・〜折には
materials.answer:
on the occasion of; when (the chance arises)

〜折に(は) marks a particular occasion or opportune moment for doing something — 'when, on the occasion of'. 上京の折には = when you come up to Tokyo; お近くにお越しの折は = should you happen to be nearby. It attaches to a noun + の or a plain-form verb and belongs to polite, somewhat formal speech, often in greetings and invitations. It tends to mark a good or fitting occasion.
materials.reading: おりに・おりには
materials.notes:
折に is polite and formal, typical of set greetings; for a neutral 'when', 時に is plainer.

It usually marks a fitting or welcome occasion, not just any random moment.

Synonyms: sai-ni — 〜際に is a formal 'on the occasion of / when'; 折に is similarly polite but favors welcome, opportune occasions and set greetings.

Related: ni-atatte — 〜にあたって marks 'on the occasion of' a significant, one-off undertaking; 折に marks a fitting moment, often social or recurring.

Source references: jlptsensei, bunpro

materials.prompt: 恐らく
materials.answer:
probably; most likely; in all likelihood

恐らく marks the speaker's fairly confident conjecture — 'probably / most likely'. It usually pairs with a following だろう, でしょう, or に違いない. 恐らく間に合わないだろう = we probably won't make it in time. It is more formal than たぶん and often leans toward a serious or unfavorable guess. Despite the kanji 恐, it has nothing to do with fear.
materials.reading: おそらく
materials.notes:
恐らく normally co-occurs with だろう / でしょう / に違いない at the end of the sentence.

The kanji 恐 does not carry a sense of 'fear' here; the word simply means 'probably'.

Related: ni-chigai-nai — に違いない expresses near-certainty; 恐らく is a weaker, more tentative 'probably'.

Source references: jlptsensei, bunpro

materials.prompt: 恐れがある
materials.answer:
there is a risk/danger that (something undesirable may happen)

恐れがある follows a verb (dictionary form) or a noun + の and warns that there is a real risk of an undesirable outcome. It is formal and largely written — common in news reports, warnings, and forecasts. 恐れ literally means 'fear', so it points to something one would rather avoid.
materials.reading: おそれがある
materials.notes:
Used only for unwelcome outcomes; you would not say 合格する恐れがある for a hoped-for result.

Formal and written; in everyday speech かもしれない sounds more natural.

Synonyms: kanenai — かねない also flags a possible bad outcome but attaches to a verb stem and is less formal; 恐れがある reads as an objective warning.

Related: kamo-shirenai — かもしれない is a neutral 'might', for good or bad; 恐れがある specifically warns of an undesirable risk.

Source references: jlptsensei, bunpro

materials.prompt: 〜終わる
materials.answer:
to finish doing (an action all the way through)

〜終わる attaches to the ます-stem of a verb to say you finish doing that action completely — 食べ終わる = finish eating, 読み終わる = finish reading. The whole compound conjugates like an ordinary る-verb (終わった, 終わって). Use it to mark the point where an action you are carrying out is done.
materials.notes:
Attach it to the stem, not the dictionary form: 書き終わる, not 書く終わる.

This compound is about finishing an action someone performs; when a situation ends on its own (会議が終わる = the meeting ends), 終わる is just an ordinary verb, not this stem-compound.

Antonyms: hajimeru — 〜始める marks the start of an action; 〜終わる marks finishing it off.

Related: tsuzukeru — 〜続ける keeps an action going; 〜終わる brings it to completion.

Related: kakeru — 〜かけ・かける is an action left half-done; 〜終わる is one carried all the way to the end.

Source references: jlptsensei, bunpro

materials.prompt: 及び
materials.answer:
and; as well as (formal listing conjunction between nouns)

及び is a formal conjunction that joins nouns or noun phrases in the sense of 'and'. It belongs to written, official registers — application forms, laws, notices, business documents — where と or や would sound too casual. It connects items in a list, not clauses.
materials.reading: および
materials.notes:
It joins nouns, not clauses or verbs; to link whole sentences use そして or また.

Formal written register only; in conversation use と instead of 及び.

Related: matawa — 又は is the same formal register but means 'or' (choose one); 及び joins items together as 'and'.

Related: aruiwa — あるいは offers an alternative ('or; or else'); 及び adds items to the same list.

Source references: jlptsensei, bunpro

materials.prompt: およそ
materials.answer:
roughly; approximately; generally; (with a negative) utterly

およそ has a few uses. Before a number it means 'roughly, about': およそ千人 = about a thousand people. As a sentence adverb it means 'generally speaking, in broad terms': およそ物事には順序がある = in general, things have an order. Reinforcing a negative, it means 'utterly, not in the least': およそ現実的でない = utterly unrealistic. Context and what follows tell the senses apart.
materials.reading: およそ
materials.notes:
With a negative, およそ means 'utterly / not in the least', not 'approximately'.

Synonyms: ooyoso — おおよそ is essentially the same word in the 'roughly / approximately' sense; およそ additionally carries the emphatic 'utterly (not)' use.

Source references: jlptsensei

materials.prompt: っぱなし
materials.answer:
leaving something in a state (often through neglect); leaving it on/open/as-is

っぱなし attaches to the ます-stem and means leaving the result of an action in place — the light left on (つけっぱなし), the door left open (開けっぱなし). It usually carries a hint of carelessness: you did something and neglected to undo it. It can also describe an action that just keeps going without a break.
materials.reading: っぱなし
materials.notes:
Attach it to the stem: つけっぱなし, not つけるっぱなし.

It usually implies something was left the way it shouldn't be (negligence), unlike the neutral まま.

Related: mama — まま neutrally states a state left unchanged; っぱなし adds the nuance that leaving it that way was careless.

Source references: jlptsensei, bunpro

materials.prompt: っぽい
materials.answer:
-ish; -like; has the quality of; tends to

っぽい tacks onto a noun, adjective stem, or verb stem to say something has the quality or tendency of that word — 子供っぽい = childish, 忘れっぽい = forgetful, 安っぽい = cheap-looking. The whole compound behaves like an い-adjective. It's colloquial and often carries a mildly critical tone.
materials.reading: っぽい
materials.notes:
With a verb stem it means 'tends to / easily does' (怒りっぽい = quick to anger), not 'looks like.'

It's casual and can sound negative: 安っぽい means 'cheap-looking,' not simply 'inexpensive.'

Synonyms: mitai-da — みたいだ says something resembles or looks like another thing; っぽい says it has that quality or tendency, more casually.

Related: gachi — がち is about how often an event tends to happen; っぽい 'tends to' describes a lasting quality or trait.

Related: rashii — らしい means 'befitting / typical of'; っぽい often means the opposite — merely -ish, or not quite befitting.

Source references: jlptsensei, bunpro

materials.prompt: ～ら
materials.answer:
casual pluralizing suffix (僕ら = we, 彼ら = they)

〜ら is a casual pluralizing suffix attached to people-words and pronouns — 僕ら = we, 彼ら = they, 君ら = you (plural). It can also group demonstratives (これら = these). It sounds more informal and blunt than 〜たち.
materials.notes:
〜ら is casual and can sound rough attached to names or to others; the neutral, polite plural is 〜たち (子どもたち).

Pointing it at other people can feel dismissive (お前ら, あいつら), so use it with care.

Source references: bunpro
